**Quantization turns a continuous prediction problem into choosing among discrete symbols.** Uniform bins assign nearby numerical values to the same token. A categorical output can then represent uncertainty over bins and generate sampled futures, but it cannot distinguish values within a bin without an additional mechanism. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13438)

If the bin width is 0.2, nearest-bin rounding has error at most 0.1 for in-range values. Clipping a value outside the range can create much larger error. Narrow bins improve resolution but increase vocabulary size or reduce covered range.

Vector, lattice, or spherical quantization operates on richer latent representations rather than necessarily binning each raw return independently. It needs an encoder/codebook and a validated reconstruction path. Continuous projections retain numerical input precision; their output heads may predict a mean, a distribution, or a more flexible diffusion/flow-generated future.

**Match representation to the needed uncertainty.** A mean forecast can hide two plausible opposite outcomes. A discrete distribution can represent both but may poorly resolve rare extremes. Normalize using only history available at prediction time, and evaluate tail behavior, interval coverage, and cross-series scale changes. No tokenization family is inherently best for financial sequences. Compare reconstruction, forecasting, and decision quality under the same information constraints.

**Technical details and references.**

Discrete bins let a sequence model predict a categorical distribution over quantized values, enabling token-based likelihood/sampling but introducing resolution, range, and scaling choices. Vector or spherical quantizers encode richer latent patterns, requiring a trained encoder/codebook and reconstruction validation. Continuous projections preserve numeric input precision and use regression or probabilistic heads. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13438)

Uniform quantization has step $\Delta$ and bounded rounding error $\Delta/2$ within range; clipping outliers violates that bound. Diffusion/flow heads can represent multimodal futures at additional sampling cost.

Normalize using only available history and evaluate tail events, cross-series scale transfer, interval coverage, and calibration. A discrete vocabulary is not inherently more expressive for financial data; compare uncertainty and decision quality, not only token prediction loss.
